title: Increasing Parking Duration for Class 2 Label Scheme Vehicles in Lots for Handicapped
what_it_is: Increasing Parking Duration for Class 2 Label Scheme Vehicles in Lots for Handicapped

sections.label: Class 1 and Class 2 labels
sections.summary: Class 1 labels let drivers with physical disabilities park in accessible lots; Class 2 labels let caregivers park there for 60 minutes to help passengers board and alight.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: Class 1 labels allow drivers with physical disabilities who drive to park in accessible parking lots.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: Class 2 labels allow caregivers to park temporarily at the accessible lots for 60 minutes so that they can assist passengers with physical disabilities to board and alight.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: Once their passengers alight and are in a safe place, the caregivers are to vacate the accessible parking lots and move their vehicles to standard lots.

sections.label: Ageing population and Class 2 labels
sections.summary: Class 2 label numbers are rising with the ageing population, and 60 minutes is considered reasonable for caregivers, while lengthening it would make accessible parking harder for others.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: With our ageing population, the number of Class 2 labels issued has also been increasing significantly.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: We believe that 60 minutes provide a reasonable amount of time for caregivers to ensure that passengers with physical disabilities alight and are in a safe place.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: Lengthening the time would make it more challenging for other label holders to seek accessible parking lots.

sections.label: Deciding whether to extend 60 minutes
sections.summary: Class 2 labels let caregivers park at accessible lots for up to 60 minutes, and extending this would affect all label holders sharing the space.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: As I mentioned in my answer earlier, Class 2 labels cater to the caregivers of the disabled person, where it allows caregivers to park at an accessible parking lot for up to 60 minutes.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: We have received several suggestions from members of the public as well, and we would just like to share that in deciding whether to extend or not, we have to look at the needs and demand of all label holders because they are all sharing this shared space.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: We believe that the 60 minutes given is a reasonable time for the caregivers to board and alight the persons with disabilities, bring that person to a safe place and, following that, go back to the vehicle to park it at the standard lots.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: We feel that extending the time will create a challenging process and increase the time taken for label holders to find accessible lots.
